- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1-2% of spike magnitude.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts; apply a 1-3 day lead correction if sentiment turns sharply.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle midpoint; adjust forecast toward historical mean of recent 7-day window.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of flat sentiment.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.0% volatility buffer if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
